name: Buttermilk (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Buttermilk [Milk and milk products] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: DTU, USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: USDA FoodData Central FDC 170874 (Milk, buttermilk, fluid, cultured, lowfat)

Gebreselassie et al. 2016, Chemical composition of naturally fermented buttermilk, Int. J. Dairy Technology, doi:10.1111/1471-0307.12236 (organic acids: lactic 5.35-11.56 mg/g, citric 52-1712 ug/g, plus acetic/orotic/pyruvic/succinic detected)
McCance & Widdowson / FRIDA dairy reference values (chloride, iodine)
provenance.curation_notes: Cultured buttermilk is a fermented dairy medium: the DOMINANT carbon/energy source is lactic acid (~0.8 g/100g, ~89 mM) produced from lactose, with residual lactose (~5 g/100g, ~146 mM) the second major fermentable substrate; citrate is largely fermented to acetate/CO2/diacetyl. Rich in casein/whey amino acids (glutamate highest), Ca/K/P, riboflavin and B12. Added the previously-missing organic acids (the key gap) and amino acids Val/Phe; removed a preservative (epsilon-polylysine), a plant fura
curation_added: lactic acid (dominant organic acid / major carbon source, was absent)
citric acid (partially fermented residual, was absent)
acetic acid (Leuconostoc citrate co-metabolite, was absent)
orotic acid (characteristic bovine-milk acid, was absent)
pyruvic acid, succinic acid (trace fermentation intermediates)
lactose amount + D-galactose + D-glucose (specific sugars; current profile had generic sugars but no lactose amount)

curation_removed.name: epsilon-Polylysine
curation_removed.reason: Food-preservative/antimicrobial additive, not an intrinsic buttermilk nutrient; would inhibit microbial growth. Likely FooDB annotation artifact.

curation_removed.name: (R)-Oxypeucedanin
curation_removed.reason: Furanocoumarin from plants (parsley/citrus family); biologically implausible in a fermented dairy matrix. FooDB predicted-not-measured.

curation_removed.name: (E)-2-Phenyl-2-butenal
curation_removed.reason: Trace aroma aldehyde, not a growth nutrient; FooDB predicted flavour compound, negligible for a growth medium.

curation_removed.name: (+/-)-erythro-Isoleucine
curation_removed.reason: Redundant non-proteinogenic diastereomer artifact of L-isoleucine already captured; not a distinct nutrient.

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all = components / (components + unresolved ingredients) — the legacy metric, which counts pipeline-derived components as covered. pct_covered_source = source-stated components / (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components). Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
